doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: Registering live performances with ASCAP and royalties in Europe
summary: Palmer explains the ASCAP Performance Plus program and how European venues handle forms.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you have to do something from your end — if you’re playing at a club in New York and you have your original music in a set, are you supposed to do something to inform those organizations that you indeed have played your original music in X club on X date.

Yeah absolutely, in the U.S. you do. I’m registered with ASCAP and they have a program called the Performance Plus Awards Program. And so what you do is you fill out, you can do it once a year or twice a year. You fill out a form that says okay on this date I played these tunes at this venue, and you have a whole spreadsheet. And I think it’s retroactive about a couple of years now. Maybe it’s gotten wider. So if you just joined, if you have a record of where you played, if you’ve got programs and all that stuff so we can really track what you played and where you played. And once you submit those forms those songs, they all, in the venues, they all have an algorithm, you know based on how much they contribute, how big the venue is, you know, and the publishing deal you have with the compositions that you played, that all generates a fee that you’ll get as a royalty payment. And so depending on how much you play in the U.S. you know there’s fees that you are entitled to. Because a lot of times you know people don’t do it and that money is staying in the account of those professional PROs organizations. And it’s just sitting there drawing interest and the musicians, you know, don’t have a means to track it down. But you know in Europe it’s different. When I play a concert there as a leader the director of the venue they’ll come to me and they’ll bring the form to me. And I just write down, you know, the songs that I played. I’m sure a lot of musicians that have been to Europe and abroad have experienced that kind of thing. And so then, then you get royalties that way and you only have to fill out a form. In the U.S. it’s all done online now, I mean since I’ve been doing it it’s all been online.
